## SMAD by format and temperature

(AC, AC-B) non-winners only; n = bids. Common value: 100·mean|π_winner − π*|/20 per round with

* T=0.5: FP-CV > SP-CV > FPSB IPV > SP-APV > SPSB IPV
* T=1.0: FP-CV > SP-CV > FPSB IPV > SPSB IPV > SP-APV

## What holds at every temperature and what does not

Holds at every temperature:
* FPSB is the hardest sealed private-value format at every temperature: yes.
* FPSB > SPSB at every temperature: yes (preserved in >= 100% of within-cell bootstrap draws at every T).
* FP-CV > SP-CV at every temperature: yes (preserved in >= 76% of draws; the weakest temperature is T=0.1). Humans: FP-CV 47.59 > SP-CV 18.23, same sign.
* Direction in SPSB IPV: under-bidding dominates the deviating bids at every temperature: yes (87% / 81% / 88% under at T=0.1/0.5/1.0; humans 8% under, i.e. GPT-4o's direction is stably OPPOSITE to humans).
* Direction in SP-APV: under-bidding dominates at every temperature: yes (90% / 92% / 85% under; humans 20%).
* Kendall tau-b vs the human ranking over the three sealed formats is positive at every temperature: yes (T=0.1: +0.33, T=0.5: +1.00, T=1.0: +0.33; P(tau>0) joint 100%, 100%, 100%).
* Clock formats with n >= 30 sit below every sealed format: T=0.1: no usable clock cell; T=0.5: yes (AC, AC-B); T=1.0: yes (AC).

Does not hold / cannot be tested:
* SP-APV > SPSB IPV (the human order, 9.31 > 5.65) holds only at T=0.5 and is reversed at T=0.1, 1.0; the gaps are T=0.1: -1.90, T=0.5: +2.05, T=1.0: -0.14 SMAD points. This single adjacent swap is why tau-b over the three sealed formats drops from +1.00 at T=0.5 to +0.33 at the other temperatures, and it is the only ordering change among formats with n >= 30.
* AC-B cannot be tested at T=0.1 (n=4 non-winners, two rounds of raw JSON, no CSV) or T=1.0 (n=8); AC has no runs at T=0.1 and n=52 at T=1.0. The all-usable tau therefore uses k=3/5/4 formats at T=0.1/0.5/1.0 and is not comparable across temperatures at face value.

Magnitudes are not stable. Among formats with n ≥ 30 at every temperature the largest swing is FP-CV,
39.00 (T=0.1) → 59.99 (T=0.5), i.e. 35% of its T=0.5 value (1.54x);
SPSB IPV moves 8.69 (T=0.5) → 14.77 (T=0.1) (70% of T=0.5, 1.70x) and
SP-CV 33.53 (T=1.0) → 40.60 (T=0.5) (1.21x). Yet the between-temperature rank correlation over
those formats never falls below Spearman +0.90 / Kendall +0.80: the only reordering is the
adjacent SPSB IPV / SP-APV swap, between the two formats whose SMADs are closest. That swap is a real
reversal at T=0.1 (bid resampling restores the human order in only
2% of draws) but a coin flip at T=1.0
(44%); at T=0.5 the human order holds in
99% of draws.

**Verdict.** The cross-mechanism ordering and the direction of deviations are robust to temperature
(FPSB hardest, FPSB > SPSB, FP-CV > SP-CV, clock formats lowest where measurable, under-bidding in both
second-price formats at every T), while the magnitudes are not (swings of 6.1 SMAD
points in SPSB IPV and 21.0 in FP-CV). The one ordinal exception is the SPSB IPV vs
SP-APV order, which is concordant with humans only at T=0.5 and reverses on a
0.14–1.90-point
gap at T=0.1 and T=1.0.

## Caveats

Human-side uncertainty is reconstruction/calibration uncertainty (`analysis/reconstruction_bands.py`), not
human sampling error. LLM CIs treat bids (or CV rounds) as i.i.d. within cells. The sealed cells use the same seed bases at every temperature (FPSB IPV [1299], SPSB IPV [1299], SP-APV [1399]), so the value draws are comparable across T; the V10 clock cells pool runs with seed bases AC [1299, 1319, 1399] / AC-B [1299, 1399], whereas the T=1.0 clock cells use [1399]. Run dates: T=0.5 2026-01-06 to 2026-01-12; T=0.1 2026-01-26 to 2026-01-31; T=1.0 2026-01-26 to 2026-01-30
-- so run date (and, for the clock cells, seed base) differ alongside temperature. The CV SMAD is
profit-based with a different normalizer (20) than the private-value SMAD (25) and is never ranked against
private-value formats here. Clock cells at T=0.1 (AC none, AC-B n=4) and AC-B at T=1.0
(n=8) are too small to say anything.
